description: Two-panel composite. (a) is a TEM bright-field (BF) micrograph of the Fe–10Mn–10Al–0.7C specimen annealed at 1100 °C: large grey α-matrix grains containing dark dislocation lines and broad dark bend-contour bands, separated by a bright, slightly curved boundary band running from lower-left to upper-right. The matrix grain to the left of the band is labelled "α" in red outline; the band is labelled "κ" in orange outline with a yellow arrow pointing to it. Two scale bars are printed at the bottom of (a): "0.5 μm" (lower left) and "500 nm" (lower right). (b) contains two selected-area diffraction patterns (SADPs) side by side: the left one, labelled "α", is taken along z = [001] and shows discrete reflections around the transmitted beam marked "T"; the right one, labelled "κ", is taken along z = [1-12] and shows reflections labelled (220) and (111). Several index labels in (b) are only partially legible at the supplied resolution; no camera constant or d-spacings are printed. Taken together, (a) documents a boundary phase between two large α grains and (b) identifies that boundary phase as κ-carbide coexisting with α, supporting the claim that κ-carbide forms along α/α boundaries in specimens annealed in the 900–1200 °C range.
measured_quantities: crystallographic zone axis in (b): [001] for α and [1-12] for κ

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a TEM bright-field micrograph in which a bright, slightly curved boundary band lies between two large α matrix grains; the band is marked with an orange 'κ' label and a yellow arrow, and the adjacent grain is marked with a red 'α' label.
Two scale bars are printed on panel (a): '0.5 μm' at the lower left and '500 nm' at the lower right.
The α grains in panel (a) contain dark dislocation lines and broad dark bend-contour contrast bands, plus a dark sub-boundary/diagonal feature crossing the lower part of the image.
Panel (b) consists of two selected-area diffraction patterns placed side by side, the left labelled 'α' with zone axis z = [001], the right labelled 'κ' with zone axis z = [1-12].
The left SADP of (b) shows a discrete spot pattern; labels legible near the transmitted beam (marked 'T') include (-110) and (110).
The right SADP of (b) shows diffraction spots annotated (220) and (111); at least one additional reflection index is not fully legible.
No camera constant, d-spacing value or measured lattice parameter is printed in either diffraction pattern of (b).
The caption states that panel (a) is a BF micrograph of the boundary κ in the specimen annealed at 1100 °C and that (b) is the SADP of α and κ.

The citing text states that TEM is used to confirm κ-carbide along the α/α boundaries, and that Fig. 11(a) is the TEM BF micrograph of the specimen annealed at 1100 °C with the SADP of boundary κ-carbide and α matrix shown in Fig. 11(b).

The citing text states that κ-carbide is found along some boundaries between large α grains in the α area for annealing temperatures from 900 °C to 1200 °C, although no obvious κ-carbide is distributed in the matrix between 900 °C and 1100 °C.

The citing text states that the boundary κ-carbide is believed to form during quenching when the annealing temperature exceeds the κ-carbide dissolution temperature, which lies between 850 °C and 900 °C.

The zone axes given in (b) differ between the two phases ([001]α vs [1-12]κ); this figure does not itself state an orientation relationship between κ and α, which the citing text attributes instead to Fig. 12(b) (N–W relationship).

subfigures.description: TEM bright-field micrograph with two printed scale bars (0.5 μm lower left, 500 nm lower right). Large α grains with dark dislocation lines and bend contours; a bright, curved boundary banded phase is labelled κ (orange, yellow arrow) between α areas labelled α (red).
SADP labelled α, z = [001]: discrete spot pattern about the transmitted beam (marked T) with reflections annotated (-110) and (110); further indices partially legible.
SADP labelled κ, z = [1-12]: spot pattern with reflections annotated (220) and (111); one further index label is not fully legible at the supplied resolution.
